sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies

items.q: Match the fasting serum prolactin range to its clinical interpretation — 1) Less than 25 ug/L 2) 25 to 40 ug/L 3) 40 to 100 ug/L 4) Greater than 200 ug/L … A) Normal reference level B) Physiological elevation (sleep, stress, chest wall stimulation) C) Drug-induced or systemic conditions D) Definite prolactinoma (rule out macroprolactin)
items.exp: Fasting prolactin < 25 is normal, 25-40 is physiological, 40-100 is drug-induced/systemic, > 100 suggests adenoma, and > 200 confirms adenoma. (Book p942)

items.q: What peak physiological prolactin level can be attained during pregnancy?
items.exp: During pregnancy, prolactin levels rise physiologically and can reach up to 180 ug/L. (Book p942)

items.q: Which clinical entity is characterized by markedly elevated serum prolactin in a completely asymptomatic individual?
items.exp: Macroprolactin presents with high measured prolactin levels while the patient remains completely asymptomatic. (Book p942)

items.q: A 40-year-old male with a 4 cm giant pituitary macroadenoma has an initial serum prolactin reported as only 45 ug/L. Suspecting the Hook effect, what is the best laboratory corrective step?
opts: Perform serial dilution of the serum sample
Precipitate the sample with polyethylene glycol
Assay the sample using gel filtration chromatography
Switch from chemiluminescence to high-performance liquid chromatography
items.exp: The hook effect occurs in giant prolactinomas where antigen excess saturates assay antibodies yielding artifactually low prolactin; 1:100 serum dilution reveals the true massive elevation. (Book p942)

items.q: A prolactinoma exceeding ___ cm in maximal diameter is categorized as a giant prolactinoma.
items.exp: A prolactinoma measuring > 4 cm is designated as a giant prolactinoma. (Book p942)

items.q: Which medication is NOT listed as a pharmacological cause of hyperprolactinemia?
items.exp: Risperidone, metoclopramide, verapamil, opiates, H2 blockers, and alpha-methyldopa cause hyperprolactinemia; levothyroxine suppresses TRH and lowers prolactin. (Book p942)

items.q: A 32-year-old psychiatric patient on haloperidol develops bilateral galactorrhea. D2 receptor blockade in which central nervous system pathway produces her worsening negative symptoms?
items.exp: Conventional antipsychotics block D2 receptors in the mesolimbic pathway, worsening negative symptoms, while tuberoinfundibular blockade causes galactorrhea. (Book p942)

items.q: Following discontinuation of an offending pharmacological agent, drug-induced hyperprolactinemia typically demonstrates a good response and normalizes within:
items.exp: Drug-induced hyperprolactinemia shows a good response and normalizes if the offending drug is stopped for < 72 hours. (Book p942)

items.q: How does primary hypothyroidism induce hyperprolactinemia?
opts: Elevated TRH acts as a prolactin-releasing hormone on lactotrophs
Direct thyroid hormone toxicity impairs hypothalamic dopamine release
Thyroid peroxidase autoantibodies cross-react with D2 receptors
Thyroxine clearance of renal prolactin is drastically diminished
items.exp: In primary hypothyroidism, compensatory high TRH levels stimulate lactotrophs to release prolactin. (Book p942)

items.q: Which systemic condition is NOT a recognized cause of hyperprolactinemia?
items.exp: Systemic causes of hyperprolactinemia include primary hypothyroidism, PCOS, CKD, and CLD; primary hyperparathyroidism does not elevate prolactin. (Book p942)

items.q: Assess the characteristics of prolactinomas: I Prolactinomas are the most common pituitary adenoma. II Microprolactinomas occur more frequently than macroprolactinomas.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Prolactinomas are the most common pituitary adenoma, with microprolactinomas outnumbering macroprolactinomas. (Book p942)

items.q: Metoclopramide induces prominent hyperprolactinemia because, unlike domperidone, it readily crosses the ___ barrier.
items.exp: Metoclopramide crosses the blood-brain barrier to block hypothalamic/pituitary dopamine receptors. (Book p942)

items.q: Match the condition to its prolactin diagnostic hallmark — 1) Macroprolactin 2) Hook effect … A) Elevated prolactin levels with completely asymptomatic patient B) Falsely low or mismatched prolactin in presence of a massive tumor
items.exp: Macroprolactin is high but asymptomatic; the hook effect features a large tumor with discordant prolactin. (Book p942)
